subject: Biochemistry
vignette: A 10-month-old boy is evaluated for loss of previously acquired milestones, hypotonia, and poor feeding. Serum lactate is 7.2 mmol/L and pyruvate is elevated; MRI shows symmetric T2 hyperintensities in the basal ganglia. Muscle biopsy demonstrates reduced NADH dehydrogenase activity.
question: Decreased activity of which of the following electron transport chain components is most likely responsible?
explanation_correct: Complex I (NADH dehydrogenase) transfers electrons from NADH to coenzyme Q and pumps protons across the inner mitochondrial membrane. Its deficiency produces Leigh syndrome with developmental regression, hypotonia, basal ganglia lesions, and lactic acidosis.

explanation_incorrect.B: Complex II is succinate dehydrogenase, which oxidizes FADH2-linked substrate; its deficiency is associated with paraganglioma and would not selectively reduce NADH dehydrogenase activity.
explanation_incorrect.C: Complex III transfers electrons from coenzyme Q to cytochrome c and would not selectively reduce NADH dehydrogenase activity.
explanation_incorrect.D: Complex IV is cytochrome c oxidase, which reduces oxygen to water; it is not NADH dehydrogenase.
explanation_incorrect.E: ATP synthase uses the proton gradient to phosphorylate ADP and does not oxidize NADH.

educationalObjective: Complex I is NADH dehydrogenase; its deficiency causes Leigh syndrome with lactic acidosis and basal ganglia lesions.
